chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn al-Abd al-A'la, from 'Ibad ibn Sulayman, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I entered upon him, and with him were Abu Bassir, Maysara, and a number of his companions. When I took my seat, he turned his face towards me and said: O Sadir, know that our Wali (Master/Imam) worships Allah while standing and sitting, sleeping and alive, and dead.
I said: May I be your ransom, we understand how he worships Allah while standing, sitting, and alive, but how does he worship Allah while sleeping and dead?

He said: When our Wali places his head to sleep, when the time for prayer comes, two angels are assigned to him who were created in the earth, did not ascend to the heaven, nor see its kingdom. They pray beside him until he awakens, and Allah records the reward of their prayer for him. One rak'ah of their prayer equals a thousand prayers of human beings.

And when Allah takes his soul, his two angels ascend to the heaven and say: O our Lord, Your servant (so-and-so) has ceased [from worship] and completed his term. You are more knowing than us about this, so grant us permission to worship You in the horizons of Your heaven and the extremities of Your earth.

Then Allah reveals to them: Indeed, in My heaven there are those who worship Me, but I have no need of their worship; rather, they are in need of it. And in My earth there are those who worship Me with the true worship, and I have not created any creation more in need of Me than they are. So descend to the grave of My Wali.

They say: O our Lord, who is that one who is blessed by Your love for him? Allah reveals to them: That is he whose pledge was taken with Muhammad, My servant and his successor, and their descendants, regarding Wilayah. Descend to the grave of My Wali (so-and-so) and pray beside him until I resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection.
The two angels descend and pray at the grave until Allah resurrects him, and He records the reward of their prayer for him. One rak'ah of their prayer equals a thousand prayers of human beings.
Sadir said: May I be your ransom, O son of Allah's Messenger, is your Wali, while sleeping and dead, more devoted in worship than when he is alive and standing?
He said: Far from it, O Sadir. Our Wali will seek security from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will accept his security.

key_terms.صَلَاةُ ٱلْمَلَكَينِ: The prayer of the two angels

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam worship Allah while sleeping or after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Fadail al-Shia* highlights the unique spiritual station of the Imam, whose worship transcends physical states through the intercession of two specific angels who pray beside him during sleep and at his grave after death. The narration emphasizes that the Imam’s validity as a spiritual guide persists even in death, culminating in his role as the one who 'assures' (yujizu amanahu) divine promises on the Day of Resurrection, a concept rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the Imams' intercessory authority.

en.badr-shahin: My father (r) narrated from Sa’d bin Abdullah from Ebbad bin Sulaiman that Sadir as-Sayrafi said:

Abu Bassir, Maysara, and other individuals were with Abu Abdullah (a) when I visited him. As soon as I sat, he turned to me and said: O Sadir, our disciple worships Allah while he is standing, sitting, sleeping, alive, and dead.
I said: Allah may make me your sacrifice. We can understand how he worships Allah while he is standing, sitting, and alive. But how is it when he is asleep and dead?

He (a) said: When the time of the prayer comes while our disciple is asleep, two angels whom were created in the earth and had never ascended to the heavens or seen the kingdom there will offer prayers next to him so as to awaken him. Allah will record the reward of the prayers of these two angels for that disciple. A single rak’a that is offered by these angels is equal to one thousand prayers that are offered by people.

When Allah seizes the soul of our disciple, his two angels ascend to the heavens and say: ’O our Lord, Your servant (so-and-so) has withdrawn from worship and taken in full his life. You, however, are more knowledgeable with this matter than we are. Allow us to worship you in the horizons of Your heavens and the extremes of Your lands.’

Allah, then, says to them -in a form of revelation-, ’In My heavens, there are many who worship Me while I am not in need for their worship. In fact, it is they who are in need for worshipping Me. On My lands, likewise, there are many who worship me so properly; yet, I have not created anything that is needier for Me than they are. Hence, descend to the grave of my disciple.’

They will say, ’O our Lord, who is that one who is enjoying Your love for him?’ Allah will answer them -in a form of revelation-, ’That one is he who has put himself under the pledge of being loyal to Mohammed; My servant, his successor, and their descendants. Descend to the grave of My disciple (so-and-so) and offer prayers there until I resurrect him for the Day of Resurrection.’

The angels then descend to offer prayers at the grave until Allah resurrects him. Allah will record the reward of the prayers of these two angels for that disciple. A single rak’a that is offered by these angels is equal to one thousand prayers that are offered by people.
I said: "Allah may make me your sacrifice, son of Allah’s Messenger. In his sleep and death, your disciple worships Allah in a way better than it is in his life and waking."
He (a) said: No, Sadir. This is too far (from the truth). On the Day of Resurrection, our disciple will seek security -for others, probably- from Allah and Allah will grant him (that security)."
